📡 Iran will continue path of resistance, avenging martyred Leader: FM Araghchi

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says the movement to avenge the martyrdom of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei will continue, stressing that the country will resist aggression and pressure by relying on independence, domestic capabilities and national dignity.

Speaking at a meeting with guests at the 40th International Islamic Unity Conference in Tehran on Friday, Araghchi said the Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei’s martyrdom after seven decades of struggle had opened a new phase of resistance. He said Iran would neither forgive nor forget the assassination.
​
The foreign minister said recent conflicts showed that attempts to undermine Iran’s social cohesion and force political change had failed. Adversaries sought insecurity and submission, but Iran’s political system remained intact, forcing them to negotiate, he added.
​
Recent war exposed limits of US regional bases
​
Araghchi said the latest war demonstrated that US bases in the region could not guarantee their security. He argued that Washington primarily supported the Israeli regime. Iran targeted US positions in response to acts of aggression, he said, describing the move as legitimate self-defense.
​
Iran relies on domestic defense capabilities
​
The minister said the conflict demonstrated Iran’s reliance on domestic defense capabilities, particularly its missile program. He said Iranian forces struck US positions despite interception efforts, while the response strengthened Iran’s standing among Muslim peoples and appreciation for supporters.
​
Iran’s achievements linked to martyred Leader’s guidance
​
Araghchi attributed Iran’s achievements to the leadership and guidance of its martyred Leader Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei over four decades. He said the martyred Leader taught self-reliance, resistance and confidence in diplomacy, emphasizing dignity and national interests. Iran preserved its territory despite three wars with major powers, the minister noted.
​
Iran will not accept ceasefire violations
​
On post-war diplomacy, Araghchi said Iran would not accept ceasefire violations and would respond to attacks. He said sanctions would not force Iran to surrender its independence or national interests.
​
Iran seeks stronger relations with Islamic countries
​
Araghchi said Iran seeks stronger relations with Islamic countries, especially neighbors, including Egypt, Lebanon, Turkey, Iraq, Pakistan, and Afghanistan. He emphasized mutual respect and cooperation, saying Iran’s approach to the Muslim world is centered on unity and vigilance against divisions.

In terms of the impact on the markets, this could look somewhat similar to 2021: there will be more money in the system, bond yields will move lower, and stocks and crypto will get even more fuel for further growth.
So the market’s fate depends on this.

But it’s still too early to celebrate the start of a new bull run. BTC has hit resistance around $81,000 — several key levels converge there at once. If the market manages to establish itself above that level, the next area of interest could very well be $95,000–$100,000.

But if it fails to break through and the inflow of big money starts to fade, the current +30% could turn out to be just a very strong bounce followed by a natural correction.

But for the first time in a long while, Bitcoin’s growth is being driven not only by expectations, but by real money and macroeconomic factors.
